blocks.x: Shrink analytics on a transaction spine — inventory shrink down 18% and investigations down to evidence, not suspicion
a pharmacy retail chain whose shrink number was negotiated at year-end rather than managed any day before that. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline quarter counted the negotiation: 2.3% shrink on high-value categories, loss-prevention reports built from exception rules so noisy that store teams ignored them, and investigations that began and ended with suspicion.
POS, inventory and staff-scheduling data lived apart, so a pattern that needed all three — the refund without the return, the void after the shift change — stayed invisible.

We built the transaction spine: POS events, inventory movements, schedule and camera metadata resolved to one store-hour model, shrink patterns detected as structures rather than thresholds, and case files assembled with the full evidence chain for investigation teams. The noise floor dropped because the signal improved, and the audits stopped being conversations.
